definition: the subjects and content taught in a school or course
example: Coding has been added to the primary school curriculum.

definition: the ability to read and write
example: Adult literacy rates have improved significantly in the region.

definition: required by a rule or law
example: In many countries, education is compulsory until the age of sixteen.

definition: relating to skills needed for a particular job
example: Vocational courses prepare students for careers in trades such as plumbing.

definition: the process of judging someone's knowledge or ability
example: Continuous assessment reduces the pressure of final exams.

definition: the ability to analyse information carefully and form reasoned judgements
example: Debating clubs help students develop critical thinking.

definition: continuing to learn throughout your life, not only at school
example: Rapid technological change makes lifelong learning essential.

definition: to officially join a course, school or university
example: More adults are enrolling in online degree programmes.

definition: to make someone want to do something, especially something that needs effort
example: Good teachers motivate students to keep learning outside the classroom.

definition: influence from people of your own age to behave in a certain way
example: Peer pressure can lead teenagers to take unnecessary risks.

definition: a new idea, method or product, or the use of new ideas
example: Technological innovation has transformed the way we shop.

definition: the use of machines and computers to do work previously done by people
example: Automation has replaced many routine factory jobs.

definition: the newest and most advanced
example: The hospital uses cutting-edge equipment to diagnose heart disease.

definition: no longer used because something newer exists
example: Many skills taught a generation ago are now obsolete.

definition: the right to keep your personal life and information to yourself
example: Many users worry about the privacy of their online data.

definition: careful watching of people, especially by authorities
example: The increase in camera surveillance has divided public opinion.

definition: an important discovery or development
example: The vaccine was a major breakthrough in medical science.

definition: a set of rules a computer follows to solve a problem or make a decision
example: Social media algorithms decide which posts appear in your feed.

definition: the ability to connect to the internet or other systems
example: Rural areas still suffer from poor internet connectivity.

definition: able to continue without damaging the environment or using up resources
example: Cities need more sustainable forms of transport.

definition: gas or other substances sent into the air
example: Electric buses help to cut carbon emissions in city centres.

definition: able to be replaced naturally, so it will not run out
example: Renewable energy now supplies a third of the country's electricity.

definition: the cutting down of large areas of forest
example: Deforestation destroys the habitats of thousands of species.

definition: the variety of plants and animals in a particular area
example: Wetlands support remarkable biodiversity.

definition: the amount of carbon dioxide released by a person's or organisation's activities
example: Eating less meat is one way to reduce your carbon footprint.

definition: the protection of nature, animals or historical places
example: Wildlife conservation projects depend heavily on donations.

definition: all the living things in an area and the way they affect each other
example: Plastic waste is damaging marine ecosystems.

definition: the natural home of an animal or plant
example: Many birds are losing their natural habitat to farmland.

definition: fuels such as coal, oil and gas formed from ancient plants and animals
example: The country aims to stop burning fossil fuels by 2050.

definition: a substance that makes air, water or soil dirty and harmful
example: Cars release pollutants that harm people's lungs.

definition: the condition of being extremely overweight in a way that is unhealthy
example: Childhood obesity has risen in line with fast-food consumption.

definition: involving a lot of sitting and little physical activity
example: Office workers often lead a sedentary lifestyle.

definition: the process of eating the right kind of food for good health
example: Good nutrition in early childhood supports brain development.

definition: the state of being healthy and happy
example: Green spaces in cities improve residents' wellbeing.

definition: lasting for a long time or happening repeatedly
example: Chronic stress can weaken the immune system.

definition: the average number of years a person is expected to live
example: Life expectancy has increased thanks to better healthcare.

definition: intended to stop something bad from happening
example: Investing in preventive healthcare saves money in the long term.

definition: all the people who work in a company, industry or country
example: Women now make up almost half of the workforce.

definition: the rate at which work is done or goods are produced
example: Flexible hours can increase employee productivity.

definition: the state of not having a job, or the number of people without jobs
example: Youth unemployment remains a serious problem in the region.

definition: something that encourages a person to do something
example: Tax incentives encourage companies to invest in green technology.

definition: a person who starts their own business, often taking financial risks
example: Young entrepreneurs are using social media to market their products.

definition: a period when the economy of a country is not successful
example: Many small businesses closed during the recession.

definition: the amount of time you spend working compared with time for your private life
example: Remote work has improved many employees' work-life balance.

definition: the chances of success and promotion in a job
example: A second language can improve your career prospects.

definition: an unfair situation in which some people have more money, rights or opportunities than others
example: Rising house prices have increased inequality between generations.

definition: help given by the state to people who need it, or general health and happiness
example: The welfare system supports families on low incomes.

definition: a law or set of laws made by a government
example: New legislation bans single-use plastic bags.

definition: to control an activity using rules
example: Governments should regulate the advertising of unhealthy food to children.

definition: to make sure people obey a law or rule
example: Speed limits are difficult to enforce on rural roads.

definition: to stop someone from doing something by making them afraid of the consequences
example: Some argue that longer prison sentences deter crime.

definition: to help someone return to a normal, useful life, for example after prison
example: Education programmes help to rehabilitate young offenders.

definition: a person who has committed a crime
example: Young offenders should receive education rather than harsh punishment.

definition: the basic systems a country needs, such as roads, power and water supplies
example: Investment in infrastructure creates jobs and supports growth.

definition: the process by which more people move to and live in cities
example: Rapid urbanisation has put pressure on housing and transport.

definition: a situation in which a place is too crowded, especially with traffic
example: A congestion charge has reduced traffic in the city centre.

definition: useful places or services such as shops, parks and sports centres
example: The new housing estate lacks basic amenities.

definition: containing too many people or things
example: Overcrowded classrooms make it difficult for teachers to give individual attention.

definition: the traditions, buildings and culture of a country that come from the past
example: Old buildings are an important part of a city's heritage.

definition: the process by which businesses, cultures and economies become connected around the world
example: Globalisation has made foreign products available everywhere.

definition: a range of different people or things
example: London is famous for its cultural diversity.

definition: false or inaccurate information, especially when spread widely
example: Misinformation about vaccines spread quickly online.

definition: the control of what people can read, watch or say
example: Censorship of the internet limits freedom of expression.

definition: the business of providing services for people on holiday
example: Tourism is the island's main source of income.

definition: a place to live or stay
example: Students often struggle to find affordable accommodation.

definition: to travel regularly between home and work
example: She commutes for over an hour each way.
